claim.why_it_matters: In the PDF, 'FORMAT 3' is an ordinary (non-bold, body-size) label paragraph that scopes the general rules that follow it inside 14.9.1.4 - exactly like 'FORMAT 1' / 'FORMAT 2' on pages 620 and 623, which the transcription renders as plain paragraphs. Promoting it to a level-2 markdown heading injects a phantom section into the document outline at the SAME level as '## 14.9.1.3 Syntax rules', so General rule 13) and everything after it appears to belong to a top-level section named 'FORMAT 3' rather than to 14.9.1.4, General rules. The transcription is overwhelmingly consistent the other way: 209 plain 'FORMAT n' label lines vs only 8 promoted to headings.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed against the rendered PDF at 300 dpi and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md.

(1) PDF typography, read off the glyphs directly. On the page-609 render, the 'FORMAT 3' line sits between general rule 12) and general rule 13) and is set in the SAME upright body face, SAME body size, and NON-BOLD weight as the surrounding numbered paragraphs. Compare the real headings on page 607: '14.9.1.3  Syntax rules' and '14.9.1.4  General rules' are printed BOLD and slightly larger. 'FORMAT 1' on page 607 (immediately under the bold '14.9.1.4 General rules' heading, before rule 1)) and 'FORMAT 2' on page 608 (between rule 5) and rule 6)) are printed in exactly the same plain non-bold body face as 'FORMAT 3' on page 609. The PDF therefore gives 'FORMAT 3' no heading role whatsoever - it is a label paragraph inside 14.9.1.4.

(2) Markdown. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25363, inside the page-609 anchor block, reads '## FORMAT 3'. Its two immediate siblings in the very same general-rules list are plain paragraphs: line 25290 'FORMAT 1' and line 25312 'FORMAT 2'. So the transcription is internally inconsistent WITHIN A SINGLE RULE LIST - this is a one-off error, not a deliberate convention.

(3) Consequence is structural, not cosmetic. In this file 14.9.1.3 and 14.9.1.4 are themselves emitted at level 2 ('## 14.9.1.3 Syntax rules' at line 25273, '## 14.9.1.4 General rules' at line 25288). '## FORMAT 3' is therefore a PEER of them, which closes 14.9.1.4 in the outline after general rule 12) and re-parents general rule 13) - and the page-610 figurative-constant table that completes it - into a phantom section named 'FORMAT 3'. Any section-slicing of this file (the mechanism this project relies on to cite an exact section/GR) mis-attributes ACCEPT Format 3 screen general rules.

(4) Counts in the claim verified exactly: 209 plain '^FORMAT n$' lines vs 8 heading-promoted ones (page-146 x4, page-466 x1, page-609 x1, page-680 x2). The 209-vs-8 ratio establishes plain as the transcription's own convention.

None of the rejection grounds apply: no text is missing or reflowed, this is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation, and it is not mere inline formatting - it changes the document's section hierarchy and hence which subclause a general rule belongs to.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with one correction to the claim's supporting evidence. The claim cites 'FORMAT 1 / FORMAT 2 on pages 620 and 623' as the parallel case; those FORMAT labels do exist and are plain, but they belong to the CALL statement (14.9.4.3 Syntax rules, page 620), a different section. The decisive siblings are nearer and stronger: 'FORMAT 1' on page 607 (ISO print page 577) and 'FORMAT 2' on page 608 (ISO print page 578) are the labels for the very same general-rules list of 14.9.1.4 that 'FORMAT 3' on page 609 belongs to; the PDF prints all three in identical plain non-bold body type, and the transcription renders the first two as plain paragraphs (lines 25290 and 25312) while promoting only the third to '## FORMAT 3' (line 25363). Because 14.9.1.4 is itself emitted as '## 14.9.1.4 General rules', the injected heading is its peer and detaches general rule 13) plus its page-610 continuation table from 14.9.1.4. Fix: demote line 25363 to a plain 'FORMAT 3' paragraph. Same defect class, worth sweeping in the same change: 7 further promoted 'FORMAT n' headings at page-146 (x4), page-466 (x1), and page-680 (x2), against 209 correctly-plain instances.
